issue.title: Sandbox plexmediaserver with a systemd hardening drop-in on athena
issue.description:
Sandbox plexmediaserver on athena with a systemd drop-in so a future Plex RCE cannot read Bryan's home or persist outside Plex's data dir:

`ProtectHome=yes` (would have hidden the plaintext sudo password and API keys the 2026-10-17 attacker could read), `ProtectSystem=strict` + `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/plexmediaserver /mnt/hercules/plex`, `PrivateTmp=yes`, `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `NoExecPaths=/tmp /var/tmp /dev/shm`, `RestrictSUIDSGID=yes`, `ProtectKernelModules=yes`, `ProtectKernelTunables=yes`, `LockPersonality=yes`, and `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_NETLINK`. Must be validated against hardware transcoding (`/dev/dri`, render/video groups), DLNA, library scans of /mnt/hercules, and Plex's own updater/codec downloads; check `systemd-analyze security plexmediaserver` before/after.

Evidence: research:202610/athena_plex_compromise_incident_report.md ("Preventing a repeat" #3).

task_type_fields.proposal: systemd hardening drop-in for plexmediaserver (ProtectHome, ProtectSystem=strict, PrivateTmp, NoExecPaths, ...)
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Needs testing against hardware transcoding and library scans, which the approved incident plan did not scope.

issue.creation_reason: The Plex RCE could read every world-readable file in Bryan's home, including his sudo password; ProtectHome and related systemd options would have contained it.

payload.entry: Landing verification under approved plan plan:202610/athena_plex_autoupdate_and_sandbox.md: tailnet d95f153 committed the exact hardening.conf and recovered probes; all source SHA-256 values match the recovery report, sources compile, and the installed readable drop-in matches byte-for-byte. Live 2026-10-18 systemctl confirms disabled/inactive/dead/MainPID=0 (as_found), ProtectHome=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, intended writable paths, noexec on tmp/shm and explicit media bind, empty capabilities, RestrictNamespaces=yes, ProtectProc=invisible, DevicePolicy=auto with no DeviceAllow; exposure is 3.3 versus 9.2 baseline. No bead-listed option dropped; GPU/device allowlists, W+X denial, ProcSubset=pid, SystemCallFilter and IPAddressDeny are deliberately excluded for documented GPU/JIT, proc, syscall and network compatibility. Read final completed probe/client/restore gate transcripts: all namespace checks PASS, counts 7275/835 unchanged, zero zz codecs, no UPnP mapping, zero sandbox log matches, successful lower-quality tailnet playback answer, then successful state restoration. Authenticated refresh/scan, server-side 720p/NVENC attribution and updater are N/A because local token absent; codec download not demonstrated; DLNA disabled. These satisfy the approved explicit N/A acceptance clause, not a claim of unexercised feature success. Optional fuller coverage from 8v.2 notes #1/#2 is consolidated in bob-cli-98; its missing client-details subproposal is not required to repeat the already successful fallback. The epic remains open for unrelated-to-sandbox apt collector landing repairs.
